You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Reposition the components into an up-left staircase. Keep component shape and sort by original horizontal position. First component goes at top-left (row 0, col 0). Each later component is shifted left by 2 columns relative to its original x-position (observed outputs: source left edges 0,3,6,9 -> output 0,1,2,3; source 0,4,7 -> 0,2,3; source 0,5,7 -> 0,3,3). Arrange each subsequent component so its top-left is generally at the previous component's bottom-right cell; stamp in left-to-right order, so later colors overwrite shared cells. This yields a contiguous diagonal chain. Empirical demos: (1) 1 2x2 at (0,0), 2 2x2 at (2,1), 3 2x2 at (3,2), 4 vertical length4 at (4,3) (notably first link is non-overlapping/offset down one); (2) 8 4x3 at (0,0), 7 2x2 at (3,2), 2 2x3 at (4,3); (3) 4 2x4 at (0,0), 2 vertical length5 at (1,3), 3 3x3 at (5,3). A solved test had components 7 vertical length4, 8 3x2, 6 vertical length3, 3 2x2, resulting rows 0-3 col0 7; 8 at rows3-5 cols0-1; 6 at rows5-7 col1; 3 at rows7-8 cols1-2, with later colors overwriting overlaps. The essential pattern is leftward compression by 2 columns per object and upward chaining at bottom-rights. One example's first link deviates, so use demonstrated shapes/overlap behavior as guidance rather than asserting unconditional formula.''')
